# inkmap

> Map photos of existing tattoos onto a 3D arm, find the bare skin, and try new designs on it. A Python CLI that writes one self-contained HTML viewer.

inkmap takes photos of an arm plus hand-placed control points, unwraps each photo onto a flat sleeve map, separates ink from skin, outlines the bare areas, and bakes the result into a 3D viewer page that works offline.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/urmzd/inkmap/blob/main/README.md): install, quick start, commands, project file format
- [Mapping guide](https://github.com/urmzd/inkmap/blob/main/skills/inkmap/SKILL.md): how to shoot photos, pick control points and check the result
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/urmzd/inkmap/blob/main/AGENTS.md): architecture, commands, and lessons learned

## Source

- [unwrap.py](https://github.com/urmzd/inkmap/blob/main/src/inkmap/unwrap.py): photo to sleeve map, ink extraction, bare-area detection
- [viewer.html](https://github.com/urmzd/inkmap/blob/main/src/inkmap/assets/viewer.html): the 3D viewer template
- [extract_arm.py](https://github.com/urmzd/inkmap/blob/main/scripts/extract_arm.py): builds the arm mesh from the MakeHuman base mesh

## Examples

- [Synthetic arm](https://github.com/urmzd/inkmap/tree/main/examples/synthetic): a drawn arm with a known answer
